title.en: The Yandang Mountains (Brush Talks from Dream Brook)

edition.en: The entry on the Yandang Mountains from book 24 (Miscellaneous Notes 1) of the Mengxi bitan, as given on Chinese Wikisource; one small-character pronunciation note is removed, and five misreadings in the Wikisource transcription (崯, 窮, 千, 峽, 以) are corrected to 嶮, 穹, 干, 陝, 有 against the Siku quanshu text (Kanseki Repository KR3j0092).
edition.zh: 《梦溪笔谈》卷二十四“杂志一”中记雁荡山的一则，据维基文库；删去一处小字注音，并据《四库全书》本（Kanseki Repository 汉籍库 KR3j0092）改正维基文库录文的五处误字：崯、穷、千、峡、以，分别改作险、穹、干、陕、有。

basis.en: Northern Song prose; the author died in 1095.
basis.zh: 北宋散文，作者卒于 1095 年。

note.en: Shen Kuo explains why the strange peaks of the Yandang Mountains cannot be seen from outside their valleys: they were not pushed up, but left standing when running water carried away the earth around them. It is among the earliest clear statements anywhere of erosion as a force that shapes a landscape. Notice how he checks the idea against the pillars of earth that stand in the great ravines of Chenggao and the west.
note.zh: 沈括解释雁荡诸峰为何从谷外望去都无所见：它们不是隆起的，而是谷中大水冲去沙土之后留下来的巨石。这是世界上最早清楚表述流水侵蚀塑造地貌的文字之一。留意他还用成皋、陕西一带大涧中的“立土”来印证这一想法。

excerpt.orig: 原其理，當是為谷中大水沖激，沙土盡去，唯巨石巋然挺立耳。
excerpt.en: Looking for the reason, it must be that the great waters in the valleys rushed against them and washed away all the sand and earth, leaving only the great rocks standing tall.
excerpt.zh: 原其理，当是为谷中大水冲激，沙土尽去，唯巨石岿然挺立耳。

gloss.en: Wenzhou, on the coast of southern Zhejiang.
gloss.zh: 今浙江温州。

gloss.en: Maps and registers: the geographical records kept by the state.
gloss.zh: 地图和簿册，指官方的地理记载。

gloss.en: The Dazhong Xiangfu years, 1008–1016, under Emperor Zhenzong of the Song.
gloss.zh: 宋真宗大中祥符年间（1008—1016）。

gloss.en: The Yuqing Zhaoying Palace, a vast Daoist palace at the capital Kaifeng, built 1009–1014 and burned down in 1029.
gloss.zh: 玉清昭应宫，在都城开封的巨大道观，1009—1014 年修建，1029 年焚毁。

gloss.en: A Buddhist book brought from the Western Regions, the lands beyond China’s northwest.
gloss.zh: 从西域传来的佛教典籍。

gloss.en: The arhat Nakula, one of the Sixteen Arhats who, in Buddhist tradition, stay in the world to guard the teaching.
gloss.zh: 诺矩罗，佛教十六罗汉之一。阿罗汉，修行圆满的圣者。

gloss.en: An Indian name for China, from Sanskrit.
gloss.zh: 古印度对中国的称呼，源自梵语。

gloss.en: A dragon’s pool: a deep pool under a waterfall.
gloss.zh: 湫，水潭。龙湫，瀑布下的深潭。

gloss.en: Guanxiu (832–912), a monk, poet and painter, best known for his strange, powerful portraits of the arhats.
gloss.zh: 贯休（832—912），唐末五代诗僧、画家，以所画罗汉像著称。

gloss.at: 雁蕩經行雲漠漠，龍湫宴坐雨濛濛
gloss.at_hans: 雁荡经行云漠漠，龙湫宴坐雨蒙蒙
gloss.en: 經行 is walking meditation and 宴坐 sitting meditation: the arhat walks in the clouds of Yandang and sits in the rain by the Dragon Pool.
gloss.zh: 经行，佛教徒往返散步以修行；宴坐，静坐。

gloss.en: The summit lake, said to be where wild geese rested on their autumn flight south: hence the name Yandang, Wild Goose Marsh.
gloss.zh: 山顶的湖，相传秋雁南飞时在此栖息，雁荡之名由此而来。

gloss.en: Xie Lingyun (385–433), the first great poet of Chinese landscape, governor of Yongjia (today’s Wenzhou) in 422–423.
gloss.zh: 谢灵运（385—433），山水诗的开创者，422—423 年任永嘉（今温州）太守。

gloss.en: Sheer, soaring, perilous and strange.
gloss.zh: 陡峭挺拔，险峻奇怪。

gloss.en: 干 is to touch: reaching up to the sky.
gloss.zh: 干，冲犯，触及。高入云霄。

gloss.en: 原 is to trace back: looking for the cause.
gloss.zh: 原，推究。推究其中的道理。

gloss.en: Standing tall and alone.
gloss.zh: 高大独立的样子。

gloss.en: The Greater and Lesser Dragon Pool falls; the greater drops nearly two hundred metres.
gloss.zh: 大龙湫、小龙湫两处瀑布，大龙湫落差近二百米。

gloss.en: Upright pillars of earth, and hollows like niches in the banks.
gloss.zh: 直立的土柱，和像佛龛一样凹进去的土崖。

gloss.en: Chenggao, near Xingyang in Henan, on the edge of the loess country.
gloss.zh: 成皋，在今河南荥阳一带，地处黄土地区边缘。

gloss.en: In the Song, the lands west of Shanzhou: the loess plateau of today’s Shaanxi and Gansu, where streams cut deep gullies.
gloss.zh: 宋代指陕州以西地区，即今陕西、甘肃一带的黄土高原，多深沟大壑。

gloss.en: Complete in every part, but small: a phrase from Mencius.
gloss.zh: 各部分都具备而规模较小。语出《孟子·公孙丑上》。

gloss.en: Dense forest and undergrowth.
gloss.zh: 茂密的树林和草丛。

note.en: An early, clear statement that running water carves landscapes, tested against other places as a field geologist would; a short note, but the reasoning is sound.
note.zh: 很早就清楚指出流水塑造山形，并像野外地质学家那样拿别处验证；只是一则短札，推理却很扎实。
